St. John Chrysostom comments on the destruction of the house of the wicked, saying: [His house becomes a heap, so that everyone who passes by it and looks at it and learns the reason avoids imitating him].

entries.section: 2. The ephah going forth:

paragraphs.text: 5 Then the angel that talked with me went forth, and said unto me, Lift up now thine eyes, and see what is this that goeth forth. 6 And I said, What is it? And he said, This is the ephah that goeth forth. He said moreover, This is their eye through all the earth. 7 And, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead: and there was a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah. 8 And he said, This is wickedness. And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof. 9 Then lifted I up mine eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings; for they had wings like the wings of a stork: and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heaven. 10 Then said I to the angel that talked with me, Whither do these bear the ephah? 11 And he said unto me, To build it an house in the land of Shinar: and when it is prepared, it shall be established there upon her own base.

entries.section: 2. The ephah going forth:

paragraphs.text: Again God warns us against sin, for the prophet saw an ephah going forth [6]. The ephah is the largest unit of measure (for measuring) among the Jews, and its going forth means that the standards or measures are not exact, or what we call “lack of discernment.”

entries.section: 2. The ephah going forth:

paragraphs.text: The prophet saw: “And, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead: and there was a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah. And he said, This is wickedness. And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof” [7-8].

Sin is likened to the lead that weighs down the soul to bring it down to the depths of the abyss, as it came in the song of Moses the prophet: “They sank as lead in the mighty waters” (Ex 15:10). Origen says: [It was said of the wicked that they sank in the mighty waters... but the saints do not sink but walk on the waters... since there is not in them the weight of sin that they should sink]. And St. Gregory of Nyssa says: [Each one departs according to his condition, so one goes lightly and another plunges into the waters. For virtue is a light thing that floats, and those who live it fly like a cloud and like doves, as Isaiah says (Isa 60:8)... but sin is heavy and sits upon man like lead]. And St. John Chrysostom says: [Nothing gives it wings and lifts it up like the enjoyment of righteousness and virtue].
The prophet saw the talent of lead lifted up, that is, sin was exposed before all, so that evil appeared as a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah that goes forth.

St. Didymus the Blind comments on the likening of evil, like virtue, to a woman, saying: [It is not strange that Holy Scripture calls the evil conduct and the corrupt thought and the brute force they generate by the name “woman,” as it calls evil here a woman; likewise in the Book of Proverbs it calls folly a woman. This is the text, for the wise man teaches his disciple, saying: “My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow thine ear to my understanding: that thou mayest regard discretion, and that thy lips may keep knowledge. For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil: but her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword. Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell” (Prov 5:1-5). And in the same Book of Proverbs uncleanness is likened to a woman (Prov 7:7-27)... And just as vices are likened to a woman, so also are virtues, and the wise man says of wisdom: “I loved her beauty and took her to live with me” (Wis 8:2)].

We return to the vision to find the weight of lead cast into the mouth of the woman, as though sin is often concentrated in the mouth, so man carries a tongue heavy upon the soul, by which he shatters himself and insults others, in contrast to the righteous man of whom it was said: “The tongue of the just is as choice silver” (Prov 10:2). It is as though the wicked man carries in his mouth a tongue of lead that brings out evils, while the righteous man carries a tongue of pure silver that speaks the word of God refined like silver seven times (Ps 12:6).

entries.section: 2. The ephah going forth:

paragraphs.text: The prophet continues his speech: “And, behold, there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings; and they had wings like the wings of a stork: and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heaven” [9].

The two women are a figure of two vices, perhaps theft and false swearing as in the previous vision, that is, the robbing of the right of the brethren and the right of God. As for his saying: “the wind was in their wings,” that is, their wings are full of wind or spirit, like the spirit of which the Apostle spoke: “the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience” (Eph 2:2), the evil spirit of which the Lord Christ said that when it is cast out of a man it returns, and finding the place from which it was cast out empty of all goodness and swept of everything beautiful, it comes with seven spirits more wicked than itself to dwell in him, so that the last state of that man is worse than the first (Mt 12:35; Lk 11:26).

And lest it be thought from the wings that the two women were rising toward heaven, he made clear that their wings were like the wings of a stork and not like the wings of a dove, as St. Didymus the Blind says: [For the stork according to the Law is an unclean bird (Lev 11:19; Deut 14:18) that dwells in the cypress trees (Ps 104:17). It is among the migratory birds (Jer 8:7). The stork is of two kinds: the white, Ciconia alba, spends the winter in central and southern Africa and migrates in the spring in huge numbers to Europe and Palestine and northern Syria. And the black, Ciconia higra, is found in Palestine and is common in the valley of the Dead Sea. The stork feeds on frogs and small reptiles, and if it finds none it seeks carrion and filth. St. Didymus the Blind comments on this, saying that the two women, who represent evil and symbolize Satan or the Antichrist and the speech of the heretics, live beside the graves to feed on carrion, so they are like whited sepulchres, white outwardly, and within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness (Mt 23:27). And as the stork builds its nest with filth so that its young come forth amid unclean foul odors, so he who walks in evil lives in the empty cares of the flesh. He who has the wings of the stork is drawn to graves and filth, but he who has the wings of a dove, that is, the work of the Holy Spirit who appeared in the form of a dove at the baptism of the Lord, is lifted up to heavenly things, and as St. Didymus the Blind says: [Who is this blessed one who bears the two wings of a dove that lift him to heaven above this world].

As for the going of the two women to Shinar [which is associated with Babylon (Gen 10:10)] to build a house for themselves, it signifies their desire to settle in the place where men anciently agreed to rebel against God Himself, so their tongues were confused and they entered into inner turmoil.
May we bear the two wings of a dove and not the wings of a stork, so that we flee from Babylon (Isa 48:20), where evil is, to find our rest in the Lord Himself, dwelling in His eternal embrace!

entries.section: 1. The vision of the four chariots:

paragraphs.text: 1 And I turned, and lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came four chariots out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of brass. 2 In the first chariot were red horses; and in the second chariot black horses; 3 and in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses. 4 Then I answered and said unto the angel that talked with me, What are these, my lord? 5 And the angel answered and said unto me, These are the four spirits of the heavens, which go forth from standing before the LORD of all the earth. 6 The black horses which are therein go forth into the north country; and the white go forth after them; and the grisled go forth toward the south country. 7 And the bay went forth, and sought to go that they might walk to and fro through the earth: and he said, Get you hence, walk to and fro through the earth. So they walked to and fro through the earth. 8 Then cried he upon me, and spake unto me, saying, Behold, these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.

It seems that this vision is an extension of the first vision, which is in chapter one, where he saw the rider on a red horse among the myrtle trees in the shade, and behind him red, bay and white horses; but here he saw “four chariots coming out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of brass. In the first chariot were red horses; and in the second chariot black (dark) horses; and in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses” [1-3].

But the first vision signifies God's saving plan by the incarnation of the Word, who comes on a red horse after the rest of the horses have prepared the way for Him, whereas here the vision signifies God's disciplinary plan for evil outside Jerusalem and God's support of the believers against the devil and his wars.

entries.section: 1. The vision of the four chariots:

paragraphs.text: He saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains, by which he probably means Mount Moriah and the Mount of Olives, as though the chariots had gone out to the valley of Jehoshaphat, which means: “the valley where Jehovah judges or condemns,” the valley in which the Lord gathers all the nations to judge them there because of their humiliation of His people (Joel 2:3). These four divine chariots, which are “the four spirits of the heavens, which go forth from standing before the LORD of all the earth” [15], have been prepared to carry out God's disciplinary plan outside Jerusalem so that the wicked may not behold the glory of Jerusalem nor enter into it but be disciplined outside, in this world, or be eternally deprived of Jerusalem while the children of God enjoy the inner eternal glory. Perhaps for the same reason the Lord of glory comes to us on the last day on the clouds, so that the wicked do not meet with Him in His glory but see Him fearsome and terrifying, while the righteous enter with Him into the eternal wedding feast.

The two mountains surrounding the valley are “mountains of brass” [1], from which no one can escape. It was said of the Lord Christ: “his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace” (Rev 1:15); he who hides in Him and is united with Him tramples the earth under his feet and its thorns and thistles cannot touch him (Gen 3:18), crushing the curse beneath him in Christ Jesus our Lord. Thus the men of the Old and New Testaments are like two mountains of brass that crush evil in the valley of Jehoshaphat and condemn it by the Lord.

St. Didymus the Blind sees that brass signifies the teachings of the sophists and heretics, which are nothing but “sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal” (1 Cor 13:1); they do not have divine love, so there applies to them the saying of the Apostle: “Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.” And as iron signifies rebellion and rigidity, brass signifies hiding error behind appearance, like two mountains of brass—as though it befits us to flee from this valley, the valley of heretics who deceive by their words devoid of true love, lest we come under the fearful judgment of God.
As for the colors of the divine chariots, they signify God's disciplines against evil and His help to His people against the devil and his evil works:

First: The first chariot with its red horses represents the spiritual wars in which the believer strives against evil unto blood (Zech 12:4), so that evil perishes for the sake of building the inner Kingdom.
Second: The second chariot with its black (dark) horses is a sign of the death that the war brings upon the devil and the destruction of his evil works.

Third: The third chariot with its white horses follows the preceding chariot, for the death of evil is life for pure virtue. Or, as St. Didymus the Blind sees, the black horses signify the instruments of God's wrath “where evil breaks forth upon all the inhabitants of the land” (Jer 1:14), to be followed by the white horses as a sign of joy after the trial, so the believer says: “Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me. I will bear the indignation of the LORD, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness” (Mic 7:8-9). Thus, when he benefits from the disciplines of the Lord, he praises, saying: “I bless thee, O LORD, for thou hast exercised thine anger upon me for my salvation; thou hast turned back thy face and had mercy upon me” (Isa 12:1).

Fourth: The grisled and bay horses coming from the south signify the varied fruit with which the soul overflows within itself by practicing repentance after discipline, for the bride says: “Come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out” (Song 4:16).

These are the four chariots with their horses to which the divine command was given: “Get you hence, walk to and fro through the earth. So they walked to and fro through the earth. Then cried he upon me, and spake unto me, saying, Behold, these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country” [7-8]. God in His love sends forth His chariots to work His divine plan in the earth, and when the north country (Babylon), a symbol of the devil, falls under punishment, the Spirit of God is quieted concerning His children. How wonderful! He permitted the north country to be a harsh instrument of discipline for them, yet His Spirit does not settle and His heart does not rest until He sees His people returned to rest in the new Jerusalem, bearing varied fruits and an overflow of blessings without measure. It is as though God who disciplines hears our groaning and groans with our groaning, and does not rest until we rest in Him. We noticed in our study of the Book of Hosea the words of the Lord Himself who permits affliction, saying: “mine heart is turned within me, my repentings are kindled together. I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger, I will not return to destroy Ephraim: for I am God, and not man; the Holy One in the midst of thee: and I will not come in wrath” (Hos 11:8-9).

entries.section: 2. The vision of the crowning of Joshua:

paragraphs.text: 9 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 10 Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah, and of Jedaiah, which are come from Babylon, and come thou the same day, and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah; 11 then take silver and gold, and make crowns, and set them upon the head of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest; 12 and speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD: 13 even he shall build the temple of the LORD; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. 14 And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the LORD. 15 And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the LORD, and ye shall know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God.

In chapter three the command was given to take off the filthy garments so that Joshua might put on an adorned garment and a fair mitre (Zech 3:4-5), and in this there was a proclamation of our being crowned in Him; by the Cross He tore up our sins, presenting to us Himself, the mystery of righteousness and victory. But here Joshua is crowned with a crown of silver and gold, and those coming from captivity are crowned with him, as though the aim of this vision is to highlight the crowning of the Church, whose members were formerly under captivity and became citizens of the new Jerusalem. We can say that the first vision signifies the Lord Christ before His Ascension, for He was crowned on the Cross and the Church was crowned in Him, and the second vision signifies the time after the Ascension, for it has become the part of the Church to be crowned by Him and for Christ to be crowned in her inwardly. As St. Augustine said, the Lord Christ was working before the Ascension in the name of the Church hidden in Him and on her behalf, but after the Ascension He hid Himself in her that she might work on His behalf and in His name.
Note the following in this vision:

First: The name of Joshua was not mentioned among the names of those coming from captivity; he was crowned first, alone, as a type of our Lord Jesus who dwelt among us on our earth without falling under the captivity of sin, nor did the devil find a place for himself in Him. He conquered first and was crowned as the firstborn of those who sleep and ascended to His heavenly house so that by Him and in Him we may enjoy the crown.

Second: The Lord asked Zechariah the prophet to take silver and gold from Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah, of the people of the captivity, and make crowns and set them on the head of Joshua the great priest; this silver and gold had previously been seized by the enemy from Jerusalem and the house of the Lord and carried into captivity with the captives to be used for the kingdom of Babylon, and now with the return of the captives the silver and gold are returned to be used in the house of the Lord for the glory of God. It is as though man, when sin takes him captive, has his bodily, psychological and material energies turned to the account of evil, and with his return to the bosom of God he presents all these things to be instruments of righteousness for the glory of God.
Third: The names of the men who gather the silver and gold from the captives are:

entries.section: 2. The vision of the crowning of Joshua:

paragraphs.text: a. Heldai or Cheldai, which means “eternal,” and he is also called “Helem” [14], which means “health” or “strength.”
b. “Tobijah,” which means “God is good.”
c. “Jedaiah,” which means “Jehovah knows,” and he was the chief of the priests who returned from captivity (Neh 12:6).

Thus the three worked together to return to the Lord the silver and gold to be crowns of glory for the Church in her one Bridegroom Joshua. In other words, if our silver and gold are not sanctified, let us look to “eternity,” or the abiding life, that it may give us health of soul and strength of spirit, so that we set out with all our energy to present them as an offering to the Lord. As for the secret of sanctifying these energies, gifts and capabilities, it is the goodness of the Lord and His tenderness, who has compassion on us and accepts our gifts; He knows us as His children and receives us to Himself, so we come to know Him and receive Him in us. In brief, we need to grasp immortality and eternity and to receive the tenderness of God and the knowledge of Him!

Fourth: They brought the silver and gold to the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah [10] before turning them into crowns. Since the word “Josiah” means “the one who saves” and the word “Zephaniah” means “Jehovah hides or treasures”; it is as though the sanctification of our energy must be accomplished in the house of “the one who saves,” that is, the Church, the temple of the Lord our Savior, who works in us secretly within the heart, and treasures us like precious jewels prepared for eternal life. God does not want for us the outward appearances that make us lose His splendor in us, but wants for us the hidden glorious life, so that we are counted precious treasures in His eyes!

Fifth: When the silver and gold were gathered they became crowns and not one crown, all of them placed on the head of Joshua... as though every crown that a believer enjoys the Bridegroom Himself puts on. Origen says concerning the martyrs that Jesus Christ is the One who calls them to the crown and the One who fights with them and the One who receives it in them. Thus the Lord is manifested in His Church, so He counts every crown of ours as a crown for Himself. And St. Didymus the Blind says: [See how Christ the Great Priest can take upon His head the crowns of all, for all believers represent the body of the Lord Christ and His members, for it was truly said to those who make up the assembly of the Church: “Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular” (1 Cor 12:27); among these members some are active hands; and others “not slothful in business” (Rom 12:11) are the feet; and others who have a pure mind are the eyes; and some who govern well and fulfill their responsibility as they should represent the head symbolically... Therefore it is reasonable that the head of the Great Priest should receive all the crowns].

St. Didymus the Blind has another interpretation of these many crowns placed on the head of the Lord Christ, saying: [Consider how Jesus alone takes many crowns, for He fought all the wars to the end, “was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin” (Heb 4:15)].

Sixth: These crowns that were placed on the head of our Bridegroom alone He presents to us, so He gives each one crowns of many virtues, and as St. Didymus the Blind says: [It is not strange that many crowns be placed on one head, for every virtue has its crown, or rather every virtue is in itself a crown, and the perfect man possesses many crowns... as long as the virtues are bound together, he who possesses them is adorned with many crowns].

Seventh: The material of the crowns is silver and gold; silver signifies the word of God (Ps 12:6) and gold the Spirit or the heavenly life, as though it befits us to prepare ourselves for these crowns through the word of God working in us and the heavenly spiritual thought.

Eighth: What is the crown that we wear in its essence but a meeting with the Lord Himself, as was said by Isaiah the prophet: “In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty” (Isa 28:5), and as St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Lord Himself is the reward of glory, granted to those who glorify God in their bodies (1 Cor 6:20), who have the spirit of submission to the preserved opinions (of the Church) and the pious traditions].

Ninth: The Lord Christ is called in this vision the man and the Branch and the East at the same time, for in the Septuagint it was said: “Behold the man, the Branch, the East is his name.” We have previously spoken of these titles in chapter three. The following is the comment of St. Didymus the Blind on this phrase: [Thus saith the LORD of hosts: Behold the man, the Branch, the East is his name, relates to our Savior who comes into this world, for He is the man as the Son of Mary... but He is the true light and the Sun of Righteousness (the East). In agreement with this text Jeremiah says: “Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth. In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS” (Jer 23:5-6). Truly He is the Branch of righteousness that springs from David... This Branch is the Sun of Righteousness and has risen from David, He who was born of the land of David according to the flesh (Rom 1:3), as was said by Isaiah the prophet: “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious” (Isa 10:11)... “Behold the man...”.

Here He declares the Bridegroom to whom the bride belongs, so He calls Him “the man.” This is what the Apostle shows when he writes to the Corinthians: “For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Cor 11:2)... Of this man John the Baptist, the greatest of those born of women (Mt 11:11), bears witness, saying: “After me cometh a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me” (Jn 1:30), and he declared this man by saying: “He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, which standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom's voice” (Jn 3:29). This One whom the prophet shows to be “the Branch”... He is the Branch from on high, a branch of the true light, the Sun of Righteousness (Mal 4:2), who has risen for those who were in darkness and the shadow of death (Lk 1:78) to dispel the darkness and remove death so that we pass over into life (Jn 5:24). Thus we become light in the Lord, as it is written: “For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord” (Eph 5:8).

Origen comments on His being called “the East,” saying that the east is of two kinds: a true east that shines upon us, He who says: “I am the light of the world,” and a misleading east like the light of the wicked which is put out (Job 18:5). And like the light of deceitful Satan who appears in the likeness of an angel of light (2 Cor 11:4).

Tenth: It was said of the Lord Christ, “and he shall grow up out of his place” [12]; if for our sake He became the Branch, He grows up, giving us true life. As the psalmist says: “Truth shall spring out of the earth” (Ps 85:11). He came to our earth, He who is the Truth able to carry us in Him, so He lifts us from the earth and establishes in us His heavenly house, therefore He continues the saying: “and he shall build the temple of the LORD,” repeating this phrase twice, on the one hand because the number 2, as we said before, signifies “love,” so by love He lifts us from the earth and establishes us as a heavenly house and a living temple for Him, and on the other hand it declares His work with the Jews as with the Gentiles, establishing all together.

Eleventh: The temple that He builds here of believers, whether of Jewish or of Gentile origin, He sits in as king and priest at the same time, which was not possible in the temple of Solomon nor in the temple that Zerubbabel built, for the kings were of the tribe of Judah and the priests of the tribe of Levi, but in the new temple the Lord dwelt to reign over us and to be priest on our behalf. “And he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both” [13]. By His kingdom and priesthood He crushes the devil and gives peace to His people. St. Didymus the Blind says: [It is a double throne: the throne of the kingdom and the throne of the priesthood also... an all-powerful throne as it is written in Proverbs: “A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes” (Prov 20:8), and also: “Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre” (Ps 44:7; Heb 1:8), “The LORD sitteth king” (Ps 29:10). As for the priestly throne, it is written in the Epistle to the Hebrews: “For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless” (Heb 7:26) and also: “Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need” (Heb 4:16). What he calls “the throne of grace” is the throne of the holy, righteous priest without defilement. Therefore he means that He took the throne of His father David to reign forever, and of His kingdom there shall be no end (Lk 1:33), and at the same time His priesthood does not pass away (Heb 7:24)... so He rules on the double throne; He is the only One who has the throne of kingship and priesthood together].

Twelfth: He speaks of the crowns that these chiefs enjoy, that they shall be “for a memorial in the temple of the LORD” [14], and in the Septuagint he says: “they shall obtain a song in the temple of the Lord.” For victory by our Lord Jesus Christ generates in us the nature of inner praise and joy of the Spirit, so that all our life turns into a hymn of praise. St. Didymus the Blind says: [We offer the teachings of good works as a hymn of praise that we chant, and delightful thoughts rise up in us like one who strikes the lute and the tambourine. We play on the lute by receiving the teachings of asceticism: “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence” (Col 3:5), “Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus” (2 Cor 4:10), through which man becomes rejected and a slave, so that he is like the tambourine made of the skin of dead animals. With this tambourine the five wise virgins who bear shining lamps strike, as in the saying of the psalm: “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels” (Ps 68:25). These timbrels which the Hebrew women used after the exodus from Egypt and the crossing of the Red Sea, with Miriam (the prophetess), the sister of Moses and Aaron, at their head... It was not possible in a desert place like this for the Hebrew women to find a number of timbrels enough for thousands of girls, but it is certain and true that they found symbolic timbrels, these of which we speak, which is the practice of piety for many years].

entries.section: 2. The vision of the crowning of Joshua:

paragraphs.text: Thirteenth: As the Lord builds His new temple He opens the doors of work to all, for He says: “And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the LORD” [15], pointing to the Gentiles who were far off and strangers, who have become by their new life in the Lord a spiritual building in the new temple.

As it came in Isaiah: “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee... Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that the wealth of the nations may be brought unto me, and their kings led” (Isa 60:10-11).

entries.section: 1. The inquiry of the people of Bethel:

paragraphs.text: 1 And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Darius, that the word of the LORD came unto Zechariah in the fourth day of the ninth month, even in Chisleu; 2 when the people of Bethel sent Sherezer and Regemmelech, and their men, to pray before the LORD, 3 and to speak unto the priests which were in the house of the LORD of hosts, and to the prophets, saying, Should I weep in the fifth month, separating myself, as I have done these so many years?

In the fourth year of Darius the king, that is, in 518 B.C., the people were working with great zeal in rebuilding the temple and the fruit of this work had appeared clearly, as the signs of ruin began to disappear from Jerusalem, so the people of Bethel sent two delegates, Sherezer and Regemmelech, and their men, to consult the priests who were in the house of the Lord and the prophets whether, after the appearance of this new life, there was still need to practice fasting and weeping in the fifth month (the tenth day) in remembrance of the burning of the house of the Lord (Jer 52:12-13; 2 Kgs 25:8-10), or whether they should stop it. This question carried two painful pictures: that fasting represented a burden in their lives which they wished to be rid of, and that it was an end in itself and was not practiced in the spirit of inner repentance and true change. Therefore the answer came carrying a rebuke on the one hand and a revelation of the concept of true spiritual fasting on the other.

entries.section: 2. Fasting without spirit:

paragraphs.text: 4 Then came the word of the LORD of hosts unto me, saying, 5 Speak unto all the people of the land, and to the priests, saying, When ye fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh month, even those seventy years, was it a fast unto me, even to me? 6 And when ye did eat, and when ye did drink, were ye not the eaters and ye the drinkers? 7 Is not this the word which the LORD hath cried by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at rest, and the cities thereof round about her, and the south and the plain inhabited?

entries.section: 2. Fasting without spirit:

paragraphs.text: Since the question carried a sign of distress and complaint on their part because of the fasting, and also carried a kind of hypocrisy, the Lord answered them that He has no need of their fasts; they fixed this fast by their own choice and it is their right to stop it without asking, but it befitted them in their fasting to practice it in a sincere spirit, and if they stopped it to rejoice in God's work with them... In other words, whether they fasted or ate, they did not offer offerings of love to God but mere outward practices. This is what He meant by His rebuke of them: “When ye fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh month, even those seventy years, was it a fast unto me, even to me? And when ye did eat, and when ye did drink, were ye not the eaters and ye the drinkers?” [5-6].

They asked about the fast of the fifth month, and He answered them also about the fast of the seventh month, which they established in remembrance of the killing of Gedaliah, governor of Judah, a matter that led to the scattering of the remnant of the Jews after the captivity (Jer 41:1-3), and He confirmed that they fasted these two fasts and others such as the fast of the tenth month in remembrance of the first siege of Jerusalem with catapults and the fast of the fourth month in remembrance of the capture of the city in the reign of Zedekiah (Jer 39:2; 52:6-7), as though He says to them, I know your fasts throughout this period, but I do not ask for the multitude of fasts but for their quality. You practiced them without returning to the Lord and not in obedience to the commandments but merely to calm their consciences.

In their minds fasting was merely abstaining from food and not from evil, and enjoying righteousness, therefore St. Didymus the Blind says: [We must restrain the stomach with the bonds of prostrations (metanoia) with tears! But how destructive it is for a man that his fast be like those who refuse to enjoy the bread of life (Jn 6:35), that is, the enjoyment of the Body of Jesus, the true Bread that came down from heaven?!]. St. Didymus again distinguishes between two kinds of fasting, offering the testimony of Holy Scripture, saying: [Concerning good fasting it is said in Joel: “Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly” (Joel 1:14; 2:15). And in another place He declares: “Prayer is good with fasting and alms, for it delivers from death” (Tob 12:8-9). As for the bad fast, we find the wicked and unbelievers accusing the Lord, saying: “Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge?” (Isa 58:3); and the Lord answers them saying: “Is it such a fast that I have chosen?” (Isa 58:5). So whoever avoids bad food must multiply good works. Truly the Scripture says: “To deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house; when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him, and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh; then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily” (Isa 58:7-8)].

entries.section: 3. Fasting that works through repentance:

paragraphs.text: 8 And the word of the LORD came unto Zechariah, saying, 9 Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Execute true judgment, and do kindness and mercy, every man with his brother: 10 and oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, nor the stranger, nor the poor; and let none of you imagine evil against his brother in your heart. 11 But they refused to hearken, and gave a stubborn shoulder, and made heavy their ears, that they should not hear. 12 Yea, they made their heart an adamant stone, lest they should hear the law, and the words which the LORD of hosts hath sent in his spirit by the former prophets: therefore came a great wrath from the LORD of hosts. 13 And it came to pass that as he cried, and they would not hear, so they cry, and I will not hear, saith the LORD of hosts: 14 and I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the nations whom they knew not. Thus the land was desolate after them, that no man passed through nor returned: for they laid the pleasant land desolate.

The Lord assures them that His speaking about fasting after the period of seventy years of humiliation is the very speaking He addressed to them by the prophets before the captivity; He does not ask for fasts, or for eating and drinking (the feasts), as an end in themselves... “Is not this the word which the LORD hath cried by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at rest, and the cities thereof round about her, and the south and the plain inhabited?” [7]. The word of the Lord does not change in a time of distress or a time of prosperity, for He asks for the holy life, and then He accepts their fasts as well as their feasts and smells in their worship a savor of delight. Thus God does not separate spiritual conduct from spiritual worship, therefore He asks of them the following:

entries.section: 3. Fasting that works through repentance:

paragraphs.text: First: “Execute true judgment” [9]. If we offer fasting that we may enjoy God's mercies, it does not befit us to judge our brethren unjustly, lest we hear the words of the Lord: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked? Judge the lowly and the fatherless; do justice to the poor and needy” (Ps 82:2-3). Habakkuk cried to the Lord, saying: “Before me are plundering and injustice, and strife ariseth and contention lifteth itself up. Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore judgment goeth forth crooked” (Hab 1:3-4).

He began with judging truly, that is, He directed the speech to the spiritual leaders, since it befits them, before they decide on the fast or cease from it, or celebrate the joyful feast, that they review their accounts in their practical life, whether they practice justice so that God hears them and accepts their counsel, or practice injustice so that they benefit neither from fasting nor from feasts! Would that they hold fast to justice and truth, listening to the words of St. Jerome on the tongue of the Lord: [I gave you authority over My flock and over the people of God, so be judges and not wolves].

Second: “Do kindness and mercy, every man with his brother, and oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, nor the stranger, nor the poor” [9-10]. Along with commitment to justice and truth, every man is also committed to kindness and mercy with his brother. It befits us to bear the spirit of our Lord Jesus crucified, where on the Cross He proclaimed the embrace of justice and mercy together. He fulfilled the divine debt on our behalf, declaring His justice and His mercy without contradiction. So that God may smell our worship with its fasts and feasts, it befits us to walk in the spirit of truth without carelessness, and in the spirit of love and mercy without harshness or tyranny.

St. Jerome offers us an example of good conduct, saying: [Indeed, the wicked man plays many roles like one acting on a stage: when he is hungry he puts on the mask of a lion to devour, and when he seizes the possessions of others he puts on the mask of a wolf, and when he kills he puts on the mask of a killer, etc... So, with the difference, it befits the saints to have different masks, but good ones. When I give alms I am like one who puts on the mask of the tender man, and when I judge with truth I put on the mask of the good judge, and when I bear injury with humility I wear the mask of the humble... Wretched is the man who has the masks of evil, and happy is he who has varied goodness. With the same thought I say that in life we live like those who play many short roles: I put on our Lord Jesus Christ within me, so that He is the mask of truth when I judge, and the mask of sincere fatherhood when I meet the orphans, and the mask of tender love when I deal with the poor, etc...

If we wish to practice a fast acceptable to God or to celebrate a feast joyful to Him, let us care for all our brethren, especially the widow, the fatherless, the stranger and the poor, bearing love without hatred in the heart even toward our brethren who trouble us.

St. Didymus the Blind offers us spiritual concepts of the widow, the fatherless, the stranger and the poor, for the praiseworthy widow is she who has lost her wicked husband, who is Satan, to seek her true Bridegroom our Lord Jesus, and the good fatherless is he who has lost his father who begot him in sin as he hears the voice: “Forget also thine own people, and thy father's house” (Ps 45:10), so that the Lord Himself may be a father to him leading him to the heights. For it was said of God: “he relieveth the fatherless and widow” (Ps 146:9), “A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows” (Ps 68:5). He also cares for the stranger who left “idol worship,” his old homeland, to set out toward the Jerusalem above, as He cares for the poor who left everything and counted it as refuse that he might win Christ.

Thus may we set out with this holy company, the souls that were widowed to win the heavenly Bridegroom, and became fatherless to receive God as their Father, and became strangers to set out to the heavenly things, and became poor to acquire the pearl of great price!

entries.section: 3. Fasting that works through repentance:

paragraphs.text: Third: “and let none of you imagine evil against his brother in your heart” [10]. St. Didymus the Blind says: [After this teaching concerning not wronging those deprived of care and protection, Scripture strongly affirms that it befits us to forget insults, not by words only but from the depth of the heart... In the same sense we recall the saying of the Savior in the Gospel: “For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you” (Mt 6:14)].

The Lord Christ gave us the parable of the servant who owed ten thousand talents (Mt 18:23-35); since his lord forgave him his debt, it befitted him to pardon his brother, but since he did not pardon him he lost the grace of his lord. The Lord commented on the parable, saying: “So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses” (Mt 18:35).

entries.section: 3. Fasting that works through repentance:

paragraphs.text: Fourth: Obedience to the commandment and hearing the voice of the Lord, for He says: “But they refused to hearken, and gave a stubborn shoulder, and made heavy their ears, that they should not hear. Yea, they made their heart an adamant stone, lest they should hear the law, and the words which the LORD of hosts hath sent in his spirit by the former prophets: therefore came a great wrath from the LORD of hosts” [11-12]. This is the summary of all their evil: “hardness of the inner heart,” which closes the door of God's mercies in their face so that they fall under His wrath.

Concerning hearing the Law or the commandment, St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Lord who gave them the Law commanded them this worship: “Give ear, O my people, to my law” (Ps 77:1), and that they follow this call: “in his law doth he meditate day and night” (Ps 1:2)... “And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up. And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes. And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates” (Deut 6:6-8). By our obedience to the commandments given to us we are counted faithful and hearers of the Law. How could he not truly be faithful and a hearer so long as he keeps the holy words in his soul and heart and speaks of them in his house as in the way, in his sleep as in his waking?! For in his sleep he says to the One who knows all things: “When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches” (Ps 63:6). And in his waking he utters the same thing, remembering in his thought the words of our Lord, saying boldly: “O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee” (Ps 63:1). And with the same longing he says with the prophet Isaiah: “With my soul have I desired thee in the night” (Isa 26:9)].

He who does not hear the Law has “a stubborn shoulder,” that is, he turns his back to the Law in stubbornness, and as St. Didymus says: [This happens when we are rooted in evil, so we deserve the rebukes of Psalm 49: “But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth? Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee” (Ps 49:16-17)... He who turns his back to the words of the Lord ignores them without feeling, so that he turns his back on the giver of these words. They are mad and full of folly, for they insult the Lord who laid down the Law by transgressing His Law, and as the Apostle says: “Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?” (Rom 2:23)... They turn their backs to Him who speaks to them: “they have turned unto me the back, and not the face” (Jer 2:27), though it should have been on the contrary that they present the face to the Creator of all things... [Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens] (Ps 123:1), and also: “Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net” (Ps 25:15)].

He who does not hear the Law has also ears heavy of hearing, and as St. Didymus says: [The stubborn shoulder is the fruit of the ear heavy of hearing, and not the ear of the body but the ear of the soul. It was said: “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies. Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: they are like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear; which will not hearken to the voice of charmers, charming never so wisely” (Ps 58:4-6). “How could he not be stubborn and deaf who makes his ear heavy and stops it, who from his birth is a stranger to the Lord, speaking lies while in the womb?! This can also apply in a symbolic way to those who became strangers from their birth to the Church their mother, withdrew from her, preferring falsehoods from their coming out of the womb, and stopped their ears like the serpent, so their energy became the work of evil and the spreading of poison].

St. Didymus also sees that the prophet Isaiah bears witness concerning these ears of the soul that are heavy of hearing, saying: “Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed” (Isa 6:10). “For since they delight in the whirlpool of evil and unbelief which they chose for themselves, their ears became heavy and their eyes were shut and their heart became fat, so they do not hear the talk about virtue and the knowledge of the truth that is able to make them virtuous and return them to the One from whom they departed, He who is able to heal them from blindness and deafness...”].

It is to be noted in the discourse before us the affirmation of human freedom, for with their full will they refused to hear, and made their ears heavy, etc... a matter which Holy Scripture affirms in both its Testaments.

entries.section: 3. Fasting that works through repentance:

paragraphs.text: Fifth: God repays their not hearing Him with His not hearing them, for He says: “Therefore came a great wrath from the LORD of hosts. And as he cried, and they would not hear, so they cry, and I will not hear, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the nations whom they knew not. Thus the land was desolate after them, that no man passed through nor returned: for they laid the pleasant land desolate” [12-14].

God in His love threatens with wrath so that when we cry to Him: “Be not wroth very sore, O LORD” (Isa 64:8), “Wilt thou be angry with us for ever? wilt thou draw out thine anger to all generations?” (Ps 85:6), we find grace in His eyes. For the Lord in His wrath, as St. Didymus the Blind says, does not avenge Himself but punishes to make us virtuous, putting an end to sin as a disease that has afflicted us or wounds in us, for He “will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth” (2 Tim 2:4). By His wrath He reveals His care for our salvation, therefore it was said: “When my wrath cometh, I will heal him again” (Isa 7:4), as says one who was healed of his wounds: “O LORD, I will praise thee: though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away, and thou comfortedst me” (Isa 12:1). St. Didymus the Blind says: [The wrath of our Lord, since a harvest of good comes with it, is not evil but is necessary. It is the work of the Physician of souls who is “healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people” (Mt 4:23)... As a wise physician, a maker of good things, He uses a painful and hateful treatment, as the prophet bears witness... “Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words” (Isa 31:2)].

entries.section: 3. Fasting that works through repentance:

paragraphs.text: He disciplines them, declaring: “I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the nations whom they knew not” [14], though He did not scatter them at that time in all the world but permitted their captivity by Assyria and Babylon, two nations known to them at that time, which shows that the threat carried a clear prophecy of what would happen to them through their rejection of the Lord Christ and their disobedience to Him, so that they would be scattered in the whole world, among nations which they had not yet known.

What are these nations under whose captivity man falls by his rejection of faith in God but the varied evils, as the Scripture says: “Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts” (Rom 1:24), “God gave them over to a reprobate mind, because they did not like to retain God in their knowledge” (Rom 1:28). For by men's rejection of the knowledge of God the grace of God abandons them and they fall under the captivity of sins and it is said of them: “being filled with all unrighteousness” (Rom 1:29); these are the nations foreign to the nature of man whom God created in His image! Because of stubbornness the land is laid waste and its delight turns to desolation, and there is neither going nor returning in it; thus by sin the body (the land) is corrupted and the life of man turns into a life of gloom and barrenness, losing inner peace, joy of heart and spiritual fruit.

entries.section: 1. God's jealousy for Zion:

paragraphs.text: 1 And the word of the LORD of hosts came, saying, 2 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I was jealous for her with great fury. 3 Thus saith the LORD; I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth; and the mountain of the LORD of hosts the holy mountain.

While they were asking about the fast that they had imposed on themselves because of the captivity, He brings them into its depths so that they may discover the blazing flame of His love toward them. It is as though He answers their question by saying: I am a jealous God who loves you; touch My fiery love so that you too may become a blazing fire that events cannot extinguish.

entries.section: 1. God's jealousy for Zion:

paragraphs.text: The heavenly Bridegroom declares His jealousy for His people who have returned from the captivity, who had fallen under chastening because of their spiritual adultery and their deviation: "I was jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I was jealous for her with great fury... I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called a city of truth; and the mountain of the LORD of hosts the holy mountain" [3].

First: God affirms His jealousy for her even though He chastened her for a time. As St. Didymus the Blind says: [This is what our Lord, the Almighty, says: "I loved Jerusalem or Zion, for I remember her after I had rejected her and cast her out so that she became despised by strangers; I love her not with just any love, but I love her with great intensity."

He is the jealous Bridegroom who longs for the return of His bride to the house of marriage. Truly His bride despised Him, committed fornication behind Him and betrayed Him (Jer 3:2); but when she came under affliction she realized her error and said: "I will go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now" (Hos 2:7). The wonder is that her first husband does not reject her but rebukes her for the past, yet in His love He humbles Himself, saying: "I am returned unto Zion, and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem"... declaring His longing to dwell in her. In place of the ruin that came upon her He makes her a city of truth, and in place of the decline to which she had fallen He makes her His holy mountain].

St. Didymus the Blind says: [She is called anew a city of truth. Truth will no longer be a wilderness (a ruin) but a city crowded with inhabitants and with many buildings: the temple and the lofty houses, and streets and roads will be set up in it... From the spiritual side, Jerusalem represents the soul that contemplates the unseen and eternal things (for Jerusalem means vision of peace), so the soul sees peace through the mutual agreement between the virtuous life and divine love; for her part she is set aflame with the torch of love and returns to Him, and for His part He returns to her, hears her supplications and gives her what she asks, so she does not cease praying to Him... And she is called "a city of truth" because she walks according to the truth that she discovers under the shadow of the Law, and because she "searches the divine Scriptures" (Jn 5:39; 2 Tim 3:16) and so enjoys the truth].

This is the work of the jealous Bridegroom: He enters our heart and makes it Jerusalem, the city of truth, so that we enjoy the vision of peace between our souls and God, and enter into the depths of the evangelical truth and do not stop at the shadows and types of the Law.

He also raises us up as "His holy mountain," and as the Psalm says: "They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion" (Ps 124:1). He lifts us up after the decline that befell us so that by His Holy Spirit we may reach the heights, firm in Him like the mountain, so that the storms of the world and the deceptions of the devil cannot shake us.

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: 4 "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age. 5 And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof. 6 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith the LORD of hosts. 7 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; 8 And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness. 9 Thus saith the LORD of hosts; Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words by the mouth of the prophets, which were in the day that the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built. 10 For before these days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction: for I set all men every one against his neighbour. 11 But now I will not be unto the residue of this people as in the former days, saith the LORD of hosts. 12 For the seed shall be prosperous; the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things. 13 And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing: fear not, but let your hands be strong. 14 For thus saith the LORD of hosts; As I thought to punish you, when your fathers provoked me to wrath, saith the LORD of hosts, and I repented not: 15 So again have I thought in these days to do well unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: fear ye not.

It is as though God says to His people: Now there is something more important than asking whether you are to fast or to stop the fast of the captivity, namely, realizing your new position after I have established you as the new Jerusalem, the city of truth, and the new mount Zion, My holy mountain... Contemplate My gifts and My grace and hold fast to them. Whether you fast mourning or keep feast rejoicing, let this be your aim in you: that I dwell in you, so that My blessing rests upon you and you enjoy My surpassing peace.
Thus God reveals the blessings of His dwelling in us, saying:

First: "There shall yet old men and old women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age" [4]. From the literal side, when God dwells in their midst they are filled with good days and peace dwells in them; death does not surprise them in their youth, but they live to old age, full of health, as they go down to the marketplaces of the city to buy what they need, each holding his staff in his hand. From the symbolic side, the marketplaces of Jerusalem in which the elders, men and women, sit are the overflow of wisdom that flows like a river that makes glad the city of God (Ps 46:4); all can go down to it to drink from it, or enter the marketplaces to acquire it. As the wise man says: "Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets" (Prov 1:20). This wisdom is "the Person of the Lord Christ," who came down from heaven and presented Himself to us as a servant; all can acquire Him within and enjoy Him; He of whom the bride says: "By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not. I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth" (Song 3:1-2). As her heart burns with longing for her Bridegroom, she seeks "Wisdom Himself" and does not find Him beside her, so she rises through repentance from her bed and enters the Church, "the holy city," and goes about in its marketplaces and streets, and finds Him revealed within it, offering Himself to whoever seeks Him.

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Second: "And the streets of the city shall be full of boys and girls playing in the streets thereof" [5]. The presence of boys and girls also in the marketplaces, playing, indicates the tranquility that prevailed over all and the absence of war that takes joy away from old and young. As Isaiah the prophet described the messianic age: "And I will rejoice in Jerusalem, and joy in my people: and the voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her, nor the voice of crying. There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old" (Isa 65:19-20).

Along with the elders there are also children playing in the marketplaces; these are the company of the simple who have attained to "childhood" so as to live in the Lord without care, as if the marketplaces of the Church include the wisdom of the elders together with the simplicity of children, as the Lord said to His disciples: "Be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves" (Mt 10:16). And as St. Jerome says: [Be simple as a dove so that you set a snare for no one, and be wise (skilful) as a serpent so that you allow no one to set a snare before you].

St. Didymus the Blind offers us a wonderful interpretation of these simple children who play in the marketplaces of the Church, that is, the holy city: [There are also little girls and boys who have begun to play a game worthy of praise, which David played, the man whose heart was according to the Lord (Acts 13:22; 1 Sam 13:14), fulfilling the will of Him who chose him, declaring with sure confidence: "I played before the LORD" (2 Sam 6:21). We can say that the children who play in the public places (the marketplaces) of the glorious city of the Lord are people who were consecrated to the Lord from their childhood, so that with purity and deep dignity they have been joined to holy speech that is blameless (Tit 2:7-8)].

In our commentary on the Book of Exodus we saw that the boys signify the soul and the girls the body; so when a person is sanctified in his entirety he brings forth fruits for the soul and the body together. There is no longer conflict between them, but they work together by the Holy Spirit, and the fruits come as boys and girls playing together in the marketplaces of the holy city with a glorious joy that cannot be uttered.

Finally, the marketplaces of the city have included the elders together with the old women, and the boys with the girls, that is, men with women, and the old with the young... As St. Didymus the Blind says: [All have become one choir singing one hymn with one heart, as it is written in the Psalm: "Both young men, and maidens; old men, and children: let them praise the name of the LORD" (Ps 148:12-13). As she cares for the wise elders, she does not neglect the wise old women who play their role in the Church. And as the Church rejoices in the wisdom of the elders, she is also glad in the victory of the young men, for the Apostle says: "I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one" (1 Jn 2:12-14)].

This divine work in the life of all members of the Church seems impossible, for the prophet says: "Thus saith the LORD of hosts; If it be marvellous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be marvellous in mine eyes? saith the LORD of hosts?!" [6]. If the enemy had utterly destroyed Jerusalem, so that in the eyes of all it was impossible for joy to return to her, yet not in God's eyes, for "with God all things are possible" (Mt 19:26)... He restores to her her glory and her joy by His dwelling in her!

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Third: "Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; and I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness" [7-8].

The new Jerusalem does not include one choir of elders and old women and boys and girls, but one people of the Lord from the rising of the sun and its setting, for the door of salvation opens to all the nations and all become one in the Lord. This is the great blessing of God's dwelling among men and His abiding among us. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Thus saith the LORD of hosts: Behold, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country, not only the people of the circumcision but the people from all the nations who believe in the Lord who is proclaimed in the Gospel. In ancient times the people in truth were of one nation, of the Hebrews... according to the testimony of Moses: "When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the LORD's portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance" (Deut 32:8-9)... As it was said: "And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious" (Isa 11:10; Rom 15:12)... "Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people" (Deut 32:43). So this people is no longer the people of the Hebrews alone, but with them are those who worship the Lord and serve Him, as the Psalm prophesied: "All nations shall serve him" (Ps 72:11), and in another text: "All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; and shall glorify thy name" (Ps 86:9), and also: "All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee. For the kingdom is the LORD's: and he is the governor among the nations" (Ps 22:27-28)... And the Gospel proclaims the union of men from every country by recording the words of the Savior: "Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob" (Mt 8:11). This call is addressed to all parts of the world. To this may be added what was said: "The God of gods, the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof" (Ps 50:1)... When did the God of gods speak and call the earth from the east to the west? When He left the people of the circumcision because they denied the Savior, the King of kings, by saying: "We have no king but Caesar" (Jn 19:15), "His blood be on us, and on our children" (Mt 27:25). So by their crucifying the Lord Christ they fell and the worship of the letter came to an end, and the Lord was able to say to them: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen" (Mal 1:10-11)...].

Thus God restores humanity from the east and the west to be a people for Him in truth and righteousness. And what we say about humanity we say about the individual: God restores him from every blow on the right (from the east) and every blow on the left (from the west), that is, from falling under open sins and from self-righteousness, so that he may belong wholly to God, enjoying truth and righteousness in Christ Jesus.

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Fourth: As the people of God gather from all the nations with one heart, it has the strengthened, strong hands that are able through the Lord to build the temple: "Let your hands be strong, ye that hear in these days these words by the mouth of the prophets, which were in the day that the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built" [9]. St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Lord Almighty commands that the hands consecrated to Him be strong... by translating the spiritual teachings into real work, so that work is joined to word; so that the hearers of the Law are not mere hearers, but turn hearing into fruit in their works].

If we have heard from the mouths of the prophets about the founding of the house of the LORD of hosts, that is, about the divine Incarnation, for the Lord Himself calls His body a temple, then this Incarnation gives strength to our hands to work by it, so that the divine commandment is transformed in our lives into a practical life lived out. God raised up this body, as it is said: "Wisdom hath builded her house" (Prov 9:1), so that God became dwelling in our midst and gives us His heavenly resources to work for the sake of His Kingdom. And as St. Didymus the Blind says: [How should the hands of those who hear the words of the prophets not be strong, when there was born of the Virgin the One who is fit to be called "God with us" (Isa 7:14)?! In truth, when God is with us our hands are strong and we can sing with a joyful voice: "The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge" (Ps 45:11-12)... He gives us a strength that transcends nature!].

Therefore let our hands be strengthened for work, and let the words of God in us be turned into life, since the Word built Himself a house by His Incarnation, giving us power to work. He has also made of us holy living stones for the building of His holy temple, for He says: "If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we (I and my Father) will come unto him, and make our abode with him" (Jn 14:23). He makes us ourselves a dwelling for Him, or a holy temple upon which the cornerstone stands, as the Apostle says: "And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone..." (Eph 2:20)].

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: Fifth: Our meeting with the incarnate God, and His dwelling in our midst, did not only strengthen the hands with His divine resources working in us, but also cut off the spirit of despair within us and set our depths aflame with hope. For work needs not only strong hands and striving and perseverance but also a spirit full of hope in the Lord; therefore He says: "For before these days there was no hire for man, nor any hire for beast; neither was there any peace to him that went out or came in because of the affliction: for I set all men every one against his neighbour" [10]. Affliction surrounded them (Hag 1:6, 9, 11; 2:16-19), which made man like the beast, without value, so that even if the two did something it was without profit and they did not deserve a wage! Jerusalem was desolate like a wilderness and ruled by strangers, so every effort a man made availed nothing. The toil of man, like that of the beast, in his going in or coming out became without profit, which turned their life into hell, so each one went out resisting his brother for no cause; in other words, instead of each working with his brother for the building of the house of God, each felt humiliation, total loss and inner emptiness, and so turned to resisting his brothers and troubling them.

From the spiritual side, a person without his meeting with his Savior, who established His holy temple, is like the beast: he works without understanding or wisdom, and so does not deserve a wage. St. Didymus the Blind says: [Scripture rebukes those who are without mind, who are in folly, saying: "Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding" (Ps 83:9). Truly, how can there be a wage for people who do everything without understanding or reason?!].

entries.section: 2. The indwelling of blessing and peace:

paragraphs.text: This is a bitter picture of humanity apart from the work of God: it goes out to work and comes in to reckoning and finds itself in emptiness, without fruit, and not deserving reward, since each one is occupied with resisting his brother, as the Psalm says: "They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips" (Ps 12:3), and as was said by Jeremiah the prophet: "Every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders. And they will deceive every one his neighbour, and will not speak the truth: they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity" (Jer 9:4-5). But under the New Covenant Jerusalem stands on true peace and brings increasing fruits, so the toil of man and beast is no longer without wage as it was formerly. He says: "But now I will not be unto the residue of this people as in the former days, saith the LORD of hosts. But the seed of peace; the vine shall give her fruit, and the ground shall give her increase, and the heavens shall give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things: [11-12]. What a joyful picture after man was working without reason like the beast, so that he had no wage, as the soul (man) loses its fruit as the body (the beast) loses its sanctity, and each resists the other; now that the Lord dwells in him, not only does his soul enjoy the wage but his body also, and there is spiritual accord between them and he has surpassing spiritual fruit, and the earth works on his behalf as heaven does, in the Lord. As the Lord returns to him and dwells within him and establishes His kingdom in his heart, the seed of peace appears, which the Father Himself plants by His Holy Spirit, and the fruits of the Holy Spirit appear as the fruits of the true vine, and the earth (the body) gives its increase as the body bears a special sanctity and becomes instruments of righteousness for God, and heaven (the soul) gives its dew, as the grace of the Holy Spirit fills it... All these God gives to the soul that receives Him in it.

St. Didymus the Blind says: [This glorious reform was fulfilled in the spiritual sense when He came who said: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised" (Lk 4:18)... It is written: "In his days shall the righteous shine forth, and abundance of peace; his peace shall know no barriers; it shall not be for one nation but for the company of the nations." The whole earth that is subject to Him who said to His disciples and to those who desire to serve Him: "My peace I give unto you" (Jn 14:27) enjoys a great calm that is established in it, and the vine gives its fruit and the earth its increase and heaven its dew. The vine that gives its fruit is the spiritual contemplations in the truth... and the earth gives its increase, as the seed that Jesus cast into it bears thirty and sixty and a hundred (Mt 13:8, 23)... The earth presents its increase to him who sows it with tears and with sweat and sorrow, so he reaps it with joy (Ps 125:5)... "They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him" (Ps 126:5). This abundant harvest is spiritual and concerns the divine word, as Hosea the prophet commanded: "Sow to yourselves in righteousness; reap according to goodness; plow for yourselves a plowing, for it is a time to seek the Lord until He come and teach you righteousness" (Hos 10:12)... As for heaven giving its dew, we shall understand the dew when we know the heaven that gives it. Heaven is no doubt none other than he who bears the image of the heavenly man (1 Cor 15:49), whose homeland is in heaven (Phil 3:20). For it was said of those who show forth the heavenly image of the Savior: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" (Ps 18:1), and it was said of them in the great song in the Book of Deuteronomy: "Rejoice, O ye heavens, with him" (Deut 32:43), that is, rejoice with the Savior. How should they not rejoice and exult with Him when they have been formed in His image, as the Apostle says: "to be conformed to the image of his Son" (Rom 8:29), and also "we shall put on the image of the heavenly" (1 Cor 15:49)?! It is fitting for us to say that by their union in one heaven they give a heavenly dew, but each one gives his own dew, imitating Moses who said: "My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew" (Deut 32:2)].

Sixth: As the believer, by God's dwelling in his heart, comes to have these divine blessings, he becomes a heaven that gives its dew, for he is no longer a curse to others nor to himself, but is a blessing... This is what we speak of in the commentary on the end of this chapter [20-23].

entries.section: 3. Reminding them of the commandment:

paragraphs.text: 16 These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates: 17 And let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD.

Amid these blessings that come upon their lives by the Lord's dwelling in them, which seem as if impossible [9], He urges them to hold fast to the divine commandment so that they do not fall under His wrath like their fathers. "These are the things that ye shall do; Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour; execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates: and let none of you imagine evil in your hearts against his neighbour; and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD" [16-17].

Now that He is rebuilding the temple and renewing Jerusalem, His holy city, He wanted this work to be founded on truth joined to righteousness, or in other words to be based on practical truth in the lives of His children. And here we notice the following in these commandments of His:

First: He begins with our relationship with our brethren in the Lord, such as speaking with our brethren in truth, and judging with justice and peace, etc... and ends with a commandment concerning our relationship with Him, "a false oath," as if God wants our inner Jerusalem to be founded on true practical love with our brethren, yet in the Lord.

Second: He begins by speaking of "truth"; this is the foundation of true building. What is this truth with which we speak to our neighbors and by which we judge but the manifestation of the "Lord Christ" Himself in our speech as in our conduct, for He declared of Himself that He is "the truth." This truth is not preached by word only but is proclaimed with power through practical conduct in the lives of the shepherds as of the flock.

St. Didymus the Blind sees that the Lord begins His speech concerning the spiritual leaders, who must proclaim "the truth" not by theoretical intellectual knowledge alone but through a virtuous life and practical conduct. Among his words in commenting on this divine statement: [It is fitting for us to hear the words of Jesus and practice them, as He Himself declared: "Whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man" (Mt 7:24)].

[Let our deeds declare the spiritual teachings that we present; thus a man becomes "a workman that needeth not to be ashamed" (2 Tim 2:15). With this thought the Apostle writes to his disciple to keep purity, gravity, sincerity and sound speech that cannot be condemned (Tit 2:7-8). What is sound speech that cannot be condemned but practicing what we enjoin on others, and our pure fidelity to what we hold out to others concerning the faith?!].

Thus the Fathers of the Church affirmed the necessity of proclaiming the truth by practical life and its manifestation in daily conduct.
